I originally picked up this game because I was completely in love with the design of the Harbinger and the shells. On that, I wasn't disappointed at all: the shells designs are genuinely good. However, once I found my main there was very little incentive to swap, it felt tedious to try multiple shells.
As for the world, I enjoyed the open-world and the overall environements. The outer areas in particular were a highlight and exploration felt rewarding.

On the downside, I really wasn't impressed by the bosses. They lacked real charisma, a few were funny, a few looked cool, but most of them were pretty forgettable especially those in the main story. On top of that the encounters became extremly tedious toward the end of the game.

Overall I'm left with mixed feelings. I had a solid time for most of the playthrough but pushing through the very end felt like a chore.

Solid game and a huge improvement from its predecessor. While the early game starts off challenging, the mid and late game's balance leans more towards a power fantasy, especially with the lack of balance caps.
World is compact and fun to traverse, and the story is concise and efficient. Enemy variety is a little sparse, especially for the runtime of a first playthrough.
Bosses were memorable, especially on a first playthrough, and build variety is vast despite the small, but fleshed out collection of shells and weapons.

This game needs a good polish and QoL update

The core gameplay is good and fun. However, everything that is out of Open Beta content is unpolished. The number of enemies on the locations, their damage is too high, enemy attacks animation is twichy and lack of telegraphing. The last part of a game is a complete mess. Especially the final boss with balls!

I think after a year of work this game could be good. Will see.

Mortal Shell 2 has a great dark atmosphere, challenging combat, and a really satisfying feeling of progression. I especially like the world design and the way the game rewards you for exploring and learning enemy patterns. The combat feels weighty and brutal, which makes every fight more intense. Overall, it’s a great choice if you enjoy Soulslike games with a darker and more atmospheric style

Very fun game, The interconnected world feels a lot like ds 1. Also this is way better than the first game that was released which was short with less shells. You can easily spend 40 + hours in this game.

I didn't want to write a review until I got 100% achievements in the game. Overall, even though it's a souls-like, you shouldn't go in expecting Dark Souls. It's more of a game shaped by that same dna but with its own distinct identity. While I really enjoyed the graphics and combat, the lore left a bit to be desired for me. Relying solely on item descriptions and journals just doesn't cut it. On top of that, recent patches have made the game way too easy in my opinion. Despite all that I'm giving it a solid 8/10. If you're into this genre, I'd definitely recommend picking it up.

P.S. I skipped commenting on performance because I didn't run into any of the reported issues on my own rig.

This game has great graphics, the world design and story is all top notch. The core gameplay is like the uncanny valley of soulslike games however, they're close enough so your brain thinks its a soulslike game but they just havent hit the mark. The amount of times you will die due to weird camera glitches or your lock on just randomly disengaging or because you fairly dodged the trajectory of an attack only for the enemy to magnetise to your new location mid swing is more frustrating than the positive aspects of the game can redeem unfortunately, really wanted to like this game and was so hyped after playing the beta :( Inb4 "get good" a good soulslike game can kill you literally 100s of times without you feeling unfair if the mechanics are tight
Absolutly outstanding as far as Im concerned its one of the best soulslikes out there.
refreshing to see a new souls like that nailed it and also has its own identity, and brought new techniques to combat and leveling up to the mix big thumbs up

I have been having stress fun... it is ruthless and way too hard for someone like me who has never played a game like this before. I wish there were difficulty settings and a save option other than the beacons that are few and very far between. You will definitely get your moneys worth in hours played vs dollars spent due to the reasons stated above. If I'm ever able to beat this game it will be because i have spent the next 15 years dedicating my life to it... Other than this, the visuals are great and the story telling through the shells is pretty awesome. If you like these types of games I'm sure you will love this.

Amazing game. Great visuals and combat, unique abilities and weapons, executions, dismemberment, fantastic aesthetic. HOWEVER it is sadly a bit buggy... randomly reset/invisible elevators (killed a run once), weird freezing one time per session within the first 10 minutes of playing, and a crash report almost every time i quit the game. but almost perfect. Hoping they patch some bugs soon. I'm nervous I'm gonna get a crash that deletes any progress...

This game is a solid 8/10 i had a lot of fun playing it.
but i had a few minor annoyance in this game,
(the game clearly was built with NG+ in mind)

- Run backs can get pretty annoying as there's no checkpoints in dungeons, so if you die in one you'll spend 1-3 mins running back

- Glimpses being limited is a design choice i guess, at least if it didn't lock shells memories i'd be ok with it but also you can only have 2.5 out of the 8 shells upgraded max on your first playthrough which is lame

- Reseting weapons upgrade is also awful, it gets really pricey at max level (50K gloom) which is absurd for first playthrough, so you either stick to one weapon or farm a lot of gold for your next weapon (materials haven't been an issue for me) EDIT: They nerfed the gloom cost to reset weapons and buffed gold so this is no longer an issue

Regardless It's still a really good souls-like that i recommend it's been a lot of fun playing it and might do the 100%, Just a few issues isn't gonna really ruin the enjoyment out of the game, except the mess that is the last boss.

Played almost 6 hours in a row. This game is AMAZING.

I hated the first Mortal Shell, this one is a huge step forward.

The combat is fluid, satisfying, challenging as any true soulslike should be. The dark fantasy world is sublime, I just love this art style so freaking much.

The open world element that allows you to travel and visit different places whenever you want is as well just great and the many shells make sure that you'll find yourself with the perfect playstyle that suits you.

It's a masterpiece. Get it, you won't regret it!

Pros:
This game is cool and fun and has nice style
There is a good story that made me want to feed glimpses to more shells to see it
There are cool interactable elements that are unlike a lot of souls-likes
The world is very open and interesting 
The power fantasy at the top end is pretty cool and fun

Cons:
The dungeons are jaquaysed so that at some point I just turned off my brain and hit stuff and I made it to the end, and retrieved everything. I can't remember the last two gate dungeons I did tbh.
There are a lot of small visual bugs or issues (water reflection is insane, none of the ghosts grab your arm during the pact animation they grab the air instead)
Some of the areas seem untested, I fell through the floor a few times.
The final boss is really bad. Feels like a boss that is in alpha testing. I hated the visuals and gameplay of it too, it had a giant ballsack and all of its moves were like if Rikishi from oldschool WWF had a sword.

all in all I did enjoy my time playing this game, but I was not happy paying full price for this unfinished game.

Amazing experience so far. Loving the exploration etc as it reminds me of Dark Souls 1. I love the combat feel and the new builds etc. They knocked it out of the park honestly. Still progressing through it and exploring everything but man does it feel and play good. If you're a souls fan like me you will LOVE This game. It's leagues better than the first one.... feels like a completely different game entirely. Sometimes it's too easy in some situations like parrying etc, but, it's overall a fantastic experience! 9/10

The first mortal shell was an amazing game, this one really feels like a complete version of it. I couldnt reccomend it enough if you like Soulsborne games. The devs listen to the community, they really care about this game and it shows.

Best Souls-like game since lies of p. Great graphics, animations, world design and gameplay variety. Some small quality of life issues such as boss runbacks, resource scarcity and minor boss bugs. Overall SOLID 8/10 with some updates and future improvements could even be a 9/10.

all in all a great game, but a lacking endgame, with a horrible final boss. and a slog gauntlet of bosses at the end. everything before that was fun. the game was wast and fun. but the end was horrible in my opinion. overall 7/10 for me. the final boss almost made me give it a 5 out of 10. but since the rest of the game was so great i cant. Hopefully they will patch the final boss to be less aids.

My first souls like game ever and I love it, the graphics are stunning on max settings, combat feels punchy and the gore is splendid. Obviously as a beginner I had to get wrecked many times until I learnt how to actually fight properly, a bit of visual bugs here and there but nothing game breaking, awesome work devs 👌🏻
Started out really strong, but fighting the same rotation of 7 enemies for 9 hours straight just kills this game. Nothing new ever happens, the level design is insanely tedious.

Fantastic entry into the "Souls-Like" genre. The game does not hold your hand, and it can get pretty intimadating at times. It is hard to tell if the map design is good or map. It is very interconnected with a lot of shortcuts to open, secrets to find, but I personally found it difficult to navigate for a while. There is just a lot of twists and turns, dungeons to complete, little corners with pieces of loot. 

That is not to speak of the artistic design. It is SUPER dreary, depressing, and just nasty, in a way. There world and people feel like there is no hope anywhere, just dread. The world looks amazing. Tall gigantic structures. Villages of crazy dancing ladies. Caves dripping of blood. Very, very cool atmosphere.

Combat is awesome, and all the shells felt very unique. Weapons, to me, were hit or miss. I found a weapon that I really enjoyed and a shell that fit my playstile. Mainly, Lazlo with the Great Martyr Blade. By the end of the game, I had put together what felt like a walking tank. But it did not start that way. You start weak and fragile. But the build up of power is awesome.

Highly recommend if you are in a souls like mood and want to play one. Huge step up from the first Mortal Shell.

The game is alright and is very interesting for the first few hours, but it quickly loses steam. I feel like more of the dungeons should have an actual goal or a mini-boss of some sort. Sometimes you would go in and just take out a homeless guy for a rock. The boss music is also very cool at first, but the majority of them sound the same, 2-3 cool bosses that I enjoyed, but most of them do the same combo over and over. Even on hard, it's a pretty easy "soul-like" game. I did like that you don't have to use any of the shell abilities, you can just dodge and parry the entire game.

Also lacks weapon variety and enemy variety. The end of the game is basically the same enemies but 10x of them, with the final boss fight being a pretty underwhelming battle considering he doesn't do many moves and just has a lot of health.

I will give the devs credit for the lighting. Out of all the UE5 games I've played, Mortal Shell 2 has the best lighting implementation.

tldr: It's not a bad game, but it needs to offer more at this price point. I don't see much replay ability after first run. I somewhat had to force myself to finish the end of the game since it was just repetitive.

The most golden shit "soulslike" joke of a game, if you ever played true souls games, this is not it.
Mediocre at best combat hidden behind good character design and environment.
Bosses levitate towards you while attacking, mobs have random stagger moments so you cant trust them and have 8 hit light combos that gotta end so you cant stop them.
Mapping mechanics are non-existent for the zones that truly matter(beacons), if you ever have to travel back to one with 5 or more spawns, good luck finding the one u stopped at last.
Builds are just spam one elem or other, most stones are useless so youre stuck either playing the OP or just having a miserable experience.
Decent start, HORRIBLE end, I'm disgusted by the last part of the game, absolute waste of anyone's time.
whilst still lacking a strong narrative or sense of direction, the gameplay is vastly improved on the first title and is downright addictive sometimes
Finished the game, started great, but the last boss and a few of the late game zones really ruin it as a whole.

There's nothing else to say other than that this game is absolutely incredible. What an absolute comeback from their first game, it is quite shocking, really really shocking!!! just wow!! - They pulled this game off from all aspects, be it exploration, boss designs, map design, map verticality, beautiful biomes and visuals, animations, voice acting and the list goes on and on!!!

I already left an amazing positive review on the demo when i played it and i will leave the same vibe into their main game.

Only thing i want the devs do is to balance a bit the south zones. normal enemies hit like a truck and i have a long HP bar lol and also some endgame bosses need to have lower dmg. I had one boss in particular who was one shotting me with a huge HP bar, so yeah i hope they adjust what needs to be adjusted!

Overall, if you love Souls games, man.....you are in one hell of a journey with this one. Have fun and congrats to the devs!

This game punches way above its weight class. There is a reason everyone was talking about it. I enjoy the shell system, the moment-to-moment gameplay, and the sense of exploration. It is also refreshing for a game to be a bit smaller in scope on purpose. It is a densely-packed world without much filler.

Also, it runs quite well on Linux.
Phenomenal game, i loved the first one and this one is a Significant improvement in all ways imaginable. One of the absolute best Soulslikes ever made

a flawed game so secute about its identity i cant not love it.
a massive step forward from mortal shell 1, i cant wait to see what the devs cook next!

I really want to love this game. It's such a marked improvement over the first installment, but the edges are just too rough for me to feel like I can. Like many others have said, the further into the game you get, the worse it becomes, and I'd like to clarify that I don't think it's the core design philosophy to blame, or even any one intended element, but rather a continuous piling on of weird jank and buggy combat that makes the game worse the further in you get. For example, the boss I fought before the final boss was a revamp of the tutorial boss , but instead of feeling like a bookend on my skill at the game improving, it felt like a coalescence of every bug and glitch every other boss had up till that point, which I can't believe was the intended experience. In that light, I just can't recommend the game as it is.

The game is very buggy so far, random crashes, sometimes when the shell dies the Harbinger get stuck and you cant attack anymore, the edges are very slippery sometimes after i executed an enemy close to an edge, I was falling into the void without being able to do anything. Amazing atmosphere overall and exiting gameplay, but the bugs ruined the experience for me
difficult at the start, but it continues to reward you as you progress, with solid gameplay.
was a good game but final half of the game was beyond slop, prefer to play roblox dark souls than this shiii

A really great souls-like and a wonderful improvement over the first Mortal Shell game.

All of the different mechanics are great and encourage experimentation; different shells with their special abilities and different skill trees (great build variety), not to mention all of the different main weapons, ranged weapons, and especially tarcores (10 tarcores that you can equip that can enhance your gameplay; poison damage, frost damage, more damage if you're under 50% health, more damage if you hit your enemy with your sidearm, etc. etc.)

There's also great variety in the level environments, and especially dungeons (which have different layouts or objectives - boss at the end, a puzzle, etc.) Many different enemies that are always fun to fight.

Parry feels good to pull off and all the different execution animations are fun to watch. The only thing that seems to be missing is a banger soundtrack, because you hear some good metal music at the beginning, but music seems to be absent throughout the game, except some boss fights.

The item collection mechanic is also neat, so that you don't end up with useless items you don't use (they become stronger to more you find).

All in all, a fun time, kudos to the devs on improving on the concepts from the first game. 9/10!

Mortal Shell got a massive glow-up, it genuinely feels like the devs were taking notes on how to craft a soulslike that's brutal but with plenty of accessibility options for those who want to tweak their experience, both in ways to make the game easier but also more difficult but rewarding. The game also has tons of really nice quality of life such as having threat indicators to show when you're getting attacked off screen, several different in-game options for how you like to parry in your souls games (Sekiro style weapon deflection or Souls shield parrying). I can't praise the design of the setting enough, the world looks absolutely horrific in the best body-horror sort of way. Also love that we're finally moving away from stamina-based combat, but you still have to fight tactically or else its super easy to get beaten out of your Shell. So far i've only unlocked around 4 or 5 Shells and they all look and have very distinct build styles which is quite exciting for repeat playthroughs.

My ONLY gripe with this game is the boss music, though it is cool, I loved Rotting Christ in the first game. And with the trailer being advertised with Behemoth, I was like "oh yeah, these boss battles are gonna be awesome," unfortunately that's not the case with Behemoth or any other similar band. AMAZING GAME, PLAY 1 AND 2!!! I am just a sucker for music, especially metal music in a world setting such as this.

Thank you for a great game.

I really liked the first Mortal Shell, but Mortal Shell 2 feels like a massive improvement in almost every way.

The gameplay is great fun, with plenty of new Shells to experiment with, expanded combat moves, executions and new weapons that give you much more variety in how you approach fights. The world is also far more interesting, with a good variety of different areas to explore. It mixes larger open combat encounters with mini-dungeons, exploration and some light puzzle solving, which keeps things feeling fresh.

I picked the game up after the latest patch, and one thing worth mentioning is that all the boss fights I've encountered have convenient beacons nearby for spawning. So, unlike some of the earlier reviews mention, there haven't been any frustratingly long walks back after dying.

And of course... the guitar is back. What more do you need?

*EDIT*

I didn't see it in patch notes but after this most recent update it seems that the bug w/the collector is fixed and now i can enjoy dying over and over again due to my lack of parrying skill :)

-----
I will GLADLY leave a positive review after they fix the game breaking / freezing bugs from this most recent patch. The game truly is a treat but the QA / testing is not there at all.

I'm sure it will get fixed...and i'll update edit my review but this is wild. Just rollback the update until its fixed or something. horrible.
Loved the first, loved the second even more. If you love soulslikes, this is one of the best.

First half: incredible. Great enemy design, fair mechanics, and dungeons/encounters everywhere you turn. A little light on bosses, with many bosses just being normal enemies with health bars.

Second half: terrible. Enemies that make you stand there and wait for their parry windows to be over, just for them to immediately do it again when you swing to punish. Bosses become health sponges that take ages to kill unless you use specific builds. Enemies that descend from nowhere and immediately blow up and knock you off ledges, killing you. Frustrating enough that I don't care to finish the game.

Tl;dr buy for 10 hours of fun and 15 hours of torture after that.

Incredible game for such a price. Lots and lots of content, each area having unique enemies, ability to try different builds.

The game however needs some sort of a balancing patch:
- Levelling up feels VERY insignificant (weapon upgrades do much more than actual character progression).
- Devs are pretty much FORCING you to replay the game multiple times either to max out all the shells or get a decent amount of skill points.
- Some dungeons feel VERY unrewarding and not worth your time. On top of that, some dungeons are bugged and prevent you from getting tarstones.
- End game is honestly a joke for how difficult it is NO MATTER what level you are or how much you've upgraded your weapon. All the enemies one-shot you and even if you manage to parry one enemy attack, 5 other enemies are already waiting their turn with you.
- The final boss was (at least to me) incredibly unsatisfying. I managed to beat him after 2 tries and my honest reaction was "huh? that's it?"

Despite its flaws I still greatly enjoyed the game. I couldn't stop playing it and was always looking forward to launching it again.
Im not gonna make some elaborate comment. Runs smoothly on max details. The combat is juicy and hefty, diffculty got bumped since beta which is great. Very pleasant experience so far.

The frist couple hours of the game are stellar. First zone is really nice to play..then things jsut slowly go down hill. Bosses randomly clip up, unblockable attacks will teleport you slightly or the boss wil track you from wild 270 angle spins...the game does not reward you for spacing. After sloggin through all the gate bosses, praying and getting lucky with some not using certain moves you get rewarded with the final boss..every boss is graphically so enticing only to be squashed by the scuffed mechanics. The sad part is I feel that the game has so much potential but hot damn does it need another layer of polish :( Zmey you took a couple years off my life and not in a fun or rewarding way.
If you are a souls like fan, wait for a sale or for a couple months post release to allow the game to be at the stage the developers sought to make.
Edit~
I have finished the game. Overall, I had a lot of fun and really enjoyed it. I will be staying with my review of negative due to the quality not matching the price point. Leaning into the scuffed aspects of the game were fine and sometimes fun but it was matched with frustrating boss fights (zmey and hexapod).

I really enjoyed the game.

Well until the very last dungeon with those bosses. Then my enjoyment pretty much fumbled and i was happy, that this torture of a dungeon was finally over.

Still recommending it, as with more patches it might improve further.

Despite its technical bugs and strict build boundaries, Mortal Shell 2 turns its limitations into its greatest strength, forcing an aggressive, intimate mastery that already has me planning my next dozen runs. Even with limited paths, finding viable loadouts like pairing lightning with specific shells delivers an absolute blast of action. However, occasional funky bugs can leave you wondering if a mechanic is intentional or just broken until you realize it is definitely a glitch. Despite those rough edges, I recommend this game because the exceptional combat depth and rewarding build variety easily overshadow the technical hiccups.

The standout feature of Mortal Shell II is its atmospheric world-building. Cold Symmetry managed to create a bleak, gloomy environment that feels truly captivating to explore. Venturing into the unknown constantly keeps you on edge, perfectly capturing that delicate balance between lingering fear and a faint sense of hope. If you love dark fantasy worlds with rich immersion, this is definitely worth picking up.

A huge step up from the first game. A must buy if you love the soul-like genre. It runs very smooth on my rig, fun combat thanks to the shells that you find and use, it brings flavor to the combat gameplay. story is actually pretty interesting, the world is beautiful in a dark metal type vibe. Highly recommend! This is a solid game.

Much better than first Mortal Shell, but still feels like pretty clunky and unwhole:

Downsides: plenty of bugs and crashes, too much of repetetative mobs, absolutely shallow lore (and absence of any script but well ok it's a souls-like after all), idiotic mobs AI, weird upgrade choices (like to lvl up tarits u like u MUST lvl up tarits u dont need), lack of weapon balace (u have only 8 main weapons in the game and at least half of them are total shit), lack of environment diversity and etc.

Upsides: the best combat impact I've ever felt in souls games, combat itself isn't bad, pretty unique art design of some bosses and the game itself

This game would be a fine choice at a ~30%+ sale and if u're hungry for souls-likes. Otherwise, nah.
While rather difficult, the atmosphere, combat and optimization of Mortal Shell 2 is far above average and well worth the money.
